claims.text: The elemental Cr coating on zirconium-alloy cladding fails prematurely in accident-relevant high-temperature steam because of Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
A thin CrN layer can be deposited between the zirconium-alloy substrate and the elemental Cr coating.
The interposed CrN layer will suppress Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
The CrN-modified system will maintain the oxidation-protection benefits of elemental Cr.
CrN is stable at high temperatures relevant to the proposed application.
The CrN layer will act as a physical barrier to element transport between zirconium alloy and Cr.
The CrN layer will act as a chemical barrier to element transport between zirconium alloy and Cr.
Inhibiting Cr–Zr diffusion will reduce the formation of deleterious intermetallic phases.
Reducing deleterious intermetallic-phase formation will preserve coating integrity.
The outer elemental Cr coating will continue to provide oxidation resistance under normal subcritical-water conditions.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the CrN-modified coating will significantly delay interdiffusion.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the CrN-modified coating will improve coating integrity during high-temperature steam exposure.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the CrN-modified coating will have longer overall durability.
The proposed coating is applicable to extended subcritical-water exposure near 300°C.
The proposed coating is applicable to steam transients up to approximately 1200°C lasting minutes.
